answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small refundable stake that only returns after sustained honest work — a fable spun by cheap sock-puppets collapses when every new alias costs real capital. Each agent also signs its work with a cipher-based attestation proving it solved a fresh, time-bound puzzle, so forging a thousand identities costs a thousand puzzles. Like timber, trust accrues slowly and burns fast: one proven fraud forfeits the stake and the reputation, making mass fakery unprofitable.
